content.title: Short Stories for Arvada's 150/250 Celebration
content.summary: The Arvada Arts and Culture Commission is launching the \"Community Voices: Short Stories for 150/250\" project to celebrate Arvada's role in Colorado's 150th anniversary and the U.S.'s 250th anniversary in 2026. Community members are invited to submit original writings reflecting on Arvada's history, which may be included in the Short Story Machine, a public kiosk that shares local stories. Submissions will be accepted starting June 1, 2026, and will contribute to a growing collection of community literature celebrating Arvada's unique identity.

![Aerial view of Olde Town Arvada with water tower, rail line and City of Arvada Arts & Culture brandi](/ImageRepository/Document?documentID=7607 "Aerial view of Olde Town Arvada with water tower, rail line and City of Arvada Arts & Culture brandi")

## Community Voices: Short Stories for Arvada’s 150/250 Celebration

The Arvada Arts and Culture Commission is inviting all community members to participate in the “Community Voices: Short Stories for 150/250” project. The project is part of Arvada’s 150/250 celebration, commemorating Colorado’s 150th anniversary of statehood and the United States’ 250th anniversary in 2026.

Through this project, community voices and stories will become part of a shared collection celebrating Arvada’s people, places and history.

We want to hear and share your memories and stories about our community — what makes Arvada special and unique, how it has impacted you, and how it fits into the history and identity of Colorado.

### Here’s How It Works

Community members are invited to submit an original piece of writing inspired by the prompt:

**“What does Arvada’s history mean to you?”**

Selected submissions will become part of the [City’s Short Story Machine](https://www.arvadaco.gov/492/Public-Art#short-story-machine) — a public literary kiosk that prints free short stories on demand for readers throughout the community.

Some examples of story and memory submissions that would fit this project include:

- Personal memories of growing up, moving to or living in Arvada
- Family stories connected to Arvada or Colorado history
- Fiction or poetry inspired by Arvada, Colorado or the community
- Reflections on meaningful places, people or moments in Arvada
- Hopes and dreams for Arvada’s future

Submissions are limited to 2,500 characters, approximately 400 words, and may be fiction, nonfiction or poetry. Writers of all ages and experience levels are encouraged to participate.

Submit your entry through [The Short Story Portal](https://arvada-arts-and-culture-commission.short-edition.com/) by clicking on the blue “Submit” button.

### [Submit Story](https://arvada-arts-and-culture-commission.short-edition.com/ "Short Story Portal")

Once your entry is submitted and reviewed, it may be added to the Short Story Machine’s growing collection of community literature. In 2026, stories will be dispensed throughout the community as the Short Story Machine travels to different businesses and public locations across Arvada.

### Project Details

Writing can be submitted beginning June 1, 2026, and submissions will continue to be accepted throughout the year. Writing submissions will be reviewed by City of Arvada staff and members of the Arts and Culture Commission before being added to the Short Story Machine library. Participants may submit stories on behalf of someone else.

The Short Story Machine is currently located at Stonebridge Retirement Community and will continue to travel to additional businesses and community locations throughout Arvada.

### About the Arvada Arts and Culture Commission

The Arvada Arts and Culture Commission (AACC) is dedicated to developing the quality, quantity and accessibility of arts and cultural experiences for the Arvada community. The Commission brings people together and strengthens Arvada’s sense of community, place and belonging by supporting and advocating for Arvada’s artistic resources and cultural activities, helping make Arvada a home for working artists.
